P1.findings_md:
What We See — P1
 (Digital Strategy & Vision, 1.18) is the lowest-scoring category in the assessment. Searches across corpam.org, NCUA filings, LinkedIn, and industry press surfaced no formally published digital transformation roadmap [E-025, E-028, E-030]. This is not evidence of strategic absence: CEO Pete Pritts publicly articulated investment in payments and technology (SO-1, SO-2), the 1% PCC model demonstrates strategic execution [E-005], and a Salesforce Sales Cloud platform was adopted in 2023 with a dedicated admin hire requiring Admin + Sales Cloud certifications [E-NEW-SF-001, confirmed via CFO Rachel Dodson and Mallory Wear LinkedIn posts]. Rather, reflects deliberate inverse-TPRM posture [IC-010]: as the trusted wholesale third-party for 533 member CUs, CACU keeps strategic plans internal.
 (Governance & Risk Appetite, 1.54) scores 1.76 points below peer median (3.30). CACU engages four external audit firms—Doeren Mayhew, CRI, Forvis Mazars, and ePay Advisors [E-160]—demonstrating governance investment. The 89% NIST CSF score (87/98 subcategories) [E-160] and §748 ISP compliance [E-131] confirm operational controls. However, no dedicated GRC platform was found for systematic finding closure tracking or risk appetite quantification. (Innovation, 1.72) shows the highest P1 evidence density: Identifee IDA (Sept 2024) [E-156] as first corporate-CU AI chatbot, Aptys co-investment (Dec 2024) [E-108], and VSoft AI-Ready Core whitepaper (Jun 2025) [E-187] confirm innovation execution.
Why It Matters — P1
P1 is the structural keystone of this assessment. At 1.41 (level 1), <2.5 triggers a connected cap on 81 P3 capability, artificially suppressing P3 from its true operational score of approximately 3.0–3.3 down to 2.58. This single mechanism accounts for a disproportionate share of CACU’s vs-peer gap. Resolving via Digital Strategy Workshop and GRC Platform is the highest-leverage action in the assessment—it closes the P1 gap AND simultaneously releases P3 to near peer parity. For the 440 non-participating member CUs evaluating CACU as a technology partner (SO-1), the absence of a published digital strategy creates ambiguity that a formal roadmap would resolve at zero technology cost.,, and form the P1 remediation stack.
P1.heading: 6.1 Pillar 1: Strategy, Governance & Culture — Score 1.41 (M1) | Peer Median ~2.15

P2.findings_md:
What We See — P2
 (Digital Marketing & Acquisition, 1.94) reflects limited digital marketing infrastructure. CACU’s member acquisition channels are LinkedIn (704 followers [E-059]), a static education calendar on corpam.org [E-052], and direct email. There is no confirmed marketing automation platform, behavioral segmentation, or digital attribution system. The 70+ credit unions at 1% PCC tier [E-005] and the broader 533-member CU network [E-130] represent CACU’s relationship base, yet a systematic digital acquisition engine targeting the 440 non-participating CUs does not yet exist. The Salesforce Sales Cloud adoption confirmed in 2023 [E-NEW-SF-001] provides the CRM foundation from which a Marketing Cloud activation would operate.
 (Onboarding & Fulfillment, 1.74) is the largest P2 gap (−1.36 vs peer median 3.10). The sso.corpam.org portal [E-217] provides access to CACU services via SSO, but the new member-CU onboarding pathway—Part 704 membership, wire setup, ACH enrollment, RTP/FedNow activation—requires manual coordination. The Salesforce Sales Cloud adopted in 2023 [E-NEW-SF-001] has not been upgraded to FSC, which includes Part-704-aware compliance workflows [E-130]. Member CU wire setup [E-114] and RTP/FedNow activation [E-010] are part of the onboarding journey that currently lacks digital orchestration. (Omnichannel Servicing, 2.05) reflects the same gap: service requests are handled via email and phone with no unified case management. (Personalization, 2.68) is the relative P2 strength, near peer median (2.80)—the 1% PCC tiered model implicitly personalizes service benefits, but not yet through the portal interface.
Why It Matters — P2
P2 is the revenue-generation pillar for SO-1. With 440 of 533 member CUs not at 1% PCC tier, P2 gaps directly constrain CACU’s ability to activate its largest growth pool. An untracked, non-personalized email-driven outreach model cannot efficiently engage 440 CUs at scale—and each CU that joins a peer’s managed-experience program (Alloya, Corporate One) is a relationship CACU may not recover. The Salesforce platform activation opportunity ( FSC + Marketing Cloud + Service Cloud + Experience Cloud) addresses all four P2 categories using the existing 2023 Salesforce org, significantly reducing procurement complexity and time-to-value. P2 is the highest-weighted pillar (30%) and directly addresses SO-1, SO-3, and SO-5.
P2.heading: 6.2 Pillar 2: Member/Customer Experience — Score 2.10 (M2) | Peer Median ~2.60

P3.findings_md:
What We See — P3
P3’s 2.58 score is structurally suppressed by the <2.5 connected cap, which applies an level 3.3 ceiling to 81 P3 capability. CACU’s genuine P3 operational score is approximately 3.0–3.3. (Core Process Automation, 2.54) reflects strong STP capability: CACU was the first corporate CU on the RTP network (Dec 2019 [E-007]), an early FedNow adopter (2024 [E-010]), and completed the Aptys ACH/wire/cash consolidation migration (Dec 2024 [E-157]). The gap to peer median (3.60) reflects the 5-track simultaneous migration [IC-004] creating transitional complexity, and the absence of cross-system orchestration above NXTsoft OmniConnect [E-165].
 (Compliance, 2.60) is operationally strong: NCUA Part 704 compliance [E-130], §748 ISP [E-131], FFIEC ACET certification [E-160], and 72-hour cyber incident notification compliance (1.833.CYBERCU, Sept 2023 [E-185]) demonstrate a comprehensive compliance infrastructure. CACU’s CLEAN regulatory record—zero enforcement actions, consent orders, LUAs, or CMPs—is a differentiating compliance posture relative to peers. The gap to peers (3.70) reflects compliance digitization (transaction monitoring automation, workflow tools) rather than compliance effectiveness. (Resilience, 2.60) is anchored by industry-leading infrastructure: three operational datacenters [E-166], Azure DRaaS with tested failover [E-178], and ISE Core Plus certification [E-131].
Why It Matters — P3
P3 is where CACU’s operational investments should translate most directly into maturity scores—and the connected cap reveals that addressing P1 is the unlock mechanism for P3. Once reaches ≥2.5 ( + ), P3 advances to approximately 3.4 without additional P3-specific technology investment. For the RTP/FedNow ecosystem growth agenda (SO-4), process automation is the operational bottleneck: as CACU onboards more member CUs to instant payment rails, exception-handling load will grow non-linearly without MuleSoft orchestration. GRC Platform directly addresses and compliance digitization. MuleSoft addresses automation scalability above OmniConnect.
P3.heading: 6.3 Pillar 3: Operations, Risk & Compliance — Score 2.58 (M3 Threshold) | Peer Median ~3.10

P4.findings_md:
What We See — P4
P4 is CACU’s strongest pillar and the assessment’s most evidence-rich area (170 of 327 evidence items). (Cybersecurity, 3.60) is the single highest-scoring category in the entire assessment. The 89% NIST CSF compliance score (87/98 subcategories, confirmed in 2025 DDR) [E-160], ISE Core Plus certification [E-131], §748 ISP compliance, ThreatAdvice cyber awareness training [E-218], AFS TrueChecks real-time fraud detection [E-218], and 1.833.CYBERCU 72-hour incident notification compliance [E-185] collectively position CACU at or near the frontier for a $4.6B corporate CU.
 (Technology Architecture, 3.46) reflects a mature, multi-vendor hybrid architecture: VSoft Wings/Vantage core [E-164], NXTsoft OmniConnect API layer [E-165], Aptys ISO 20022-certified payment hub [E-196], Pidgin RTP/FedNow connector [E-009], three operational datacenters [E-166], and Azure DRaaS [E-178]. The Apr 2025 VSoft API-first modernization [E-187] signals a cloud-ready architectural reset in progress. (Analytics & AI, 3.30—highest above-peer score at +0.50) is anchored by Identifee IDA [E-156]: the first production GenAI/RAG chatbot in the corporate CU sector (Sept 2024). NXTsoft OmniLytics provides ALM, CECL, and risk analytics [E-165]. The current strength is CACU-internal; the next differentiation layer is member-CU-facing analytics and Agentforce AI extension.
Why It Matters — P4
P4 is CACU’s competitive moat and the foundation for the entire Salesforce platform activation strategy. The existing 2023 Salesforce Sales Cloud org, combined with Azure infrastructure [E-178], NXTsoft OmniConnect APIs [E-165], and the Identifee IDA proof point [E-156], means CACU does not need to build from scratch—it needs to activate. cybersecurity leadership (3.60) must be protected as the Salesforce org expands: Shield provides the §748 ISP encryption layer for the growing PII surface. The primary driver is not operational absence but IC-010 inverse-TPRM positioning: as the trusted wholesale third-party for 533 member CUs, CACU deliberately keeps detailed public governance artifacts sparse for security reasons. However, the ABSENCE of a documented digital strategy creates two tangible risks: (1) the <2.5 connected cap suppresses 81 P3 capability scores — removing it restores P3 to ~3.4, closing the majority of CACU's peer gap in one move; (2) member CUs evaluating CACU as a technology partner have no publicly accessible transformation narrative to anchor their trust. The existing Salesforce Sales Cloud adoption (2023, E-NEW-SF-001) has not been articulated in any strategic roadmap.

A Zennify-facilitated Digital Strategy Workshop produces: (a) a formal digital maturity roadmap anchored to CACU's 5 Strategic Objectives and existing technology investments; (b) a governance framework that can be selectively published to member CUs to demonstrate strategic intent without exposing internal controls; (c) a stakeholder-ready narrative framing the 2023 Salesforce adoption, Aptys joint-ownership, and Identifee IDA as components of a coherent digital transformation.
